body.value: There are a number of government services available to anyone who faces an illness that will change their life.

Contact your general practitioner (GP) and ask for:

  • diagnosis/summary letter (or referral letters)
  • medical certificates (“certified unfit for work”) if you’re stopping work

If you have been referred to the hospital, ask your consultant or clinic for:

  • consultant letters
  • treatment plan
  • expected duration
  • functional impact

Most government supports require medical evidence (Illness Benefit, Disability Allowance, medical card assessments and so on).
If you’re working and need income support, start with employer

Ask your employer or HR department about:

  • company sick pay
  • occupational schemes
  • income protection insurance

If you think your workplace isn’t following the rules, look to the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC) for guidance on sick leave.
Apply to the Department of Social Protection for the right payment

In Ireland, most illness/disability payments run through the Department of Social Protection (DSP), usually via MyWelfare and MyGovID or your local Intreo Centre.

If you have a short-term illness and you’re temporarily unfit for work, you need to apply for Illness Benefit. You can apply online or request forms.

If you need in-person or local help, contact your local Intreo Centre.

If your illness has a long-term or permanent impact and you can’t work, you need to check:

  • Invalidity Pension (PRSI-based, long-term)
  • Disability Allowance (means-tested; also available to people who may not have enough PRSI)

If you can return to work but are not at full capacity, you can apply for Partial Capacity Benefit.

If your illness creates extra costs or you’re stuck waiting on a decision, contact the Community Welfare Service for Supplementary Welfare Allowance.

This is often the fastest route for emergency/exceptional expenses (rent issues, travel costs, essential once-off needs, and so on).

Apply for a Medical Card (or GP Visit Card)

You can apply online through the HSE portal but there are also phone and postal options.

Drugs Payment Scheme (DPS)

If you don’t have a medical card, you can apply for the Drugs Payment Scheme (DPS). The DPS caps what you pay per month for approved prescribed drugs and medicine.

Long-Term Illness (LTI) Scheme

If your condition is on the approved list, you can apply for the Long-Term Illness (LTI) Scheme. It provides certain medicines and appliances free for specific long-term conditions.
Contact Revenue to claim tax relief for medical expenses
If you’ve paid tax, you may be able to claim tax relief on qualifying health expenses.

Citizens Information (illness/disability payments and how to apply)

Get guided, case-by-case help (forms + what you qualify for).

MABS (Money Advice and Budgeting Service) contact routes

If money/debt becomes an issue.

Carer’s Allowance (DSP)

If you’re caring for someone (or will need a carer)
Set up access to online services through MyGovID and MyWelfare

Many DSP applications are easier/quicker online:
